pr_title: Add redis sentinel support to ruby part of code
pr_body:
Here is my approach to adding redis sentinel support.

It uses the newly refactored redis configuration class and addresses some of the feedback in #26571. It should also be compatible with the (slightly different) semantics in #31623, though given the combinatorial nature of the different configuration variants, I am not 100% sure :confused: 

Should be merged together with #31623, which implements the JS/streaming side of things.

~~Note: This has not been tested with a real sentinel setup yet.~~ I tested this (combined with #31623) locally with a sentinel setup and it worked flawlessly :tada: 

Closes #26571
Fixes #26565

issue_context.title: Redis Sentinel Support for Sidekiq
issue_context.body:
### Pitch

It would be really nice to have the ability to leverage systems like Redis Sentinel for redundancy/disaster recovery, especially since Sidekiq queues are stored in Redis as a permanent storage solution. As it stands now, Mastodon will _not_ automatically try to discover the master node (these are terms used by redis itself) of a Redis Sentinel deployment, resulting in writes being directed to read-only replicas. Thankfully, Sidekiq supports this itself, by passing it a list of Sentinel instances that it can use to determine the master node.

Unfortunately since Hiredis is a fairly small wrapper and I'm not overly familiar with the codebase yet, I have yet to determine the amount of work required to get this working for the cache (ideally, we also support Redis Cluster for our caching workload, but that's a separate thing imo)

### Motivation

Redis' own persistence model is a bit weak, and outright failing instances could lose data along the way. To alleviate this, Redis Sentinel could be used to automatically promote a new master node and allow fairly seamless failovers. As Mastodon grows, there's only so much vertical scaling possible, and vertical scaling offers no redundancy.
comments: A note, I am willing to try implementing this myself, but I wanted to gather some feedback/thoughts prior to getting going to increase the chances my changes can be accepted upstream and don't live forever in a fork.

review_comments: I supported using SENTINEL_PORT or something too, we should probably make sure that's the same; I don't mind using a hardcoded default port

I *knew* I missed something. Thank you so much for catching this.

I guess this is really helpful when all your sentinels use the same (non-standard) port.
Also here I think you want to use `REDIS_SENTINEL_PORT` https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/blob/main/streaming/redis.js#L34

No. As mentioned in my other comment the url needs to be something like `redis://<user>:<password>@<sentinel_master_name>/<db>` without a port number. Every sentinel could be on a different port number and the port number of the redis master is supplied by the sentinels to the application.
I don't think you can use REDIS_URL with Sentinels?

Not `REDIS_URL`, no. But the redis ruby gem allows giving a `url` parameter even when using sentinels. The hostname must be the sentinel master name, no port number. This can be handy when giving redis username and/or password.

Would also be worth checking:

```
REDIS_SENTINELS: '192.168.0.1,192.168.0.2:4000'
```

So mixed, one with port, one without.
I added this in the PR mentioned above.
